title: MacCrab Rave Revocation List (v0)
description: Schema for rave/revocations.json. Per plan §12. The list is Ed25519-signed by the offline catalog key (detached revocations.json.sig verified against catalog.pub); client tools verify the signature before consuming.

version.description: Schema version. Bumped only on breaking changes.

serial.description: Monotonic revocation-list serial. Monotonic-increment rule: every change to `revocations` (or any other field) MUST increment serial by +1, and serial MUST never decrease across two validly-signed revocations.json the client observes. Because revocations.json is Ed25519-signed, this is a SIGNED counter: a client that has seen serial N MUST reject any later-fetched, validly-signed list whose serial < N as a stale/rollback (replay) attack that would silently un-revoke a compromised plugin; a network attacker cannot forge a higher serial without the offline catalog key. Bound into the client's provenance receipt so a run can prove which revocation state was in effect — answering 'was it revoked when I ran it?' offline, forever (PLATFORM-VISION keystone). Distinct from `version` (the format version). REQUIRED going forward: /api/admin/revoke.js always emits an incremented serial; kept out of `required` here only so the pre-ceremony signed revocations.json (which predates this field) still validates. Promote to `required` in the same commit that lands the re-signed revocations.json.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the last update. Operators check this against the staleness thresholds in plan §3.9 (warning >30 days, critical >90 days).

revocations.description: List of revoked plugin versions. Operators with affected versions installed receive a hot-uninstall instruction at next install/update check.

scope.description: Which versions of plugin_id are revoked.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of the revocation. Operator-facing; shown in the dashboard.

advisory_url.description: Optional link to a public security advisory (GitHub Security Advisories, CVE entry, etc.).

decided_by.description: GitHub logins of maintainers who decided the revocation. Multi-maintainer governance (plan §13.2) requires at least 2 signers for high-impact revocations; v0 with solo maintainer is single-signer with warning.

affected_signing_identity.description: If revocation is keyed on a specific signing event (e.g., exfiltrated workflow OIDC token), record the exact identity. Operators may have other versions from a different signing event that remain valid.
